surfaces.part: ramp surface (snow slope with chevron texture)
left and right cut walls (blue-grey rock)

answer.evidence: Rows 0-47 are a large sloped snow plane, the ramp, with chevron texture. It narrows toward the bottom and ends in a dark edge line at row 47-48 where the blue-grey cut walls meet the front. Rows 48-63 are the vertical south cliff face (16 rows, uniform L=180). The stepped blue-grey walls on the left and right are the receding sides of the cut. The ramp has a clear top surface and a front face of more than 3 rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ramp has a sensible structure: blue-grey cliff edges with stepped highlights on both sides, and V-shaped streaks on the snow slope. The outline is tinted, with 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so it is not a sticker line. Visible tones per tile (8) match or exceed the references (3 for grass, 7 for paving). The weak points are flat areas and shading depth. Near-flat coverage is 29%, against 0% for both references, and the lower ramp and the margins between the streaks are large single-colour beige areas. The whole piece uses only 13 distinct colours, and the snow ramp shows about 4 lightness steps against Beodeul's 5-6. The grain is sparse and the streaks are thin, so each tile reads flatter than the grass and paving references. When in doubt, fail.

No south-facing vertical face of 3 or more rows is drawn across the ramp. The only vertical surfaces are the side wall strips, which are narrow and run alongside the slope, so the tile reads as a flat top-down ramp with side walls.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 8 visible tones per tile, above the grass (3) and close to the paving (7), and its dark edges are tinted (0% neutral), so the blue-grey cliff walls read as dark material tone rather than a black sticker line. It falls short on structure and texture. Only 13 distinct colours are used in total, and 29% of the candidate is near-flat, where both references are at 0%. In the picture the lower half of the ramp is a large flat beige/pink fill with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. The streaked scallops at the top are the only texture. Each material ramp (snow ramp, cliff wall) has about 3-4 steps, against the 5-6 steps the references carry. The measured tone count is propped up by the small wall and streak details. Overall the piece sits below the references on flat fills and shading depth, so it fails.
